rationale: C05 and C18 are the closest because they convey greetings or best wishes from the President and the American people to another nation's people on a commemorative occasion. Those similarities are conventional diplomatic language and a generic ceremonial function, however, not distinctive or extensive enough to show that either supplied a concrete, material drafting template. C13 shares only a similarly routine expression of sentiment between nations. No candidate reproduces the child's compact anniversary-telegram structure or sufficiently distinctive wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On the occasion of this national holiday ... the people of the United States join me in sending to the peoples of the Soviet Union our best wishes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: extend greetings and felicitations from the people of the United States to the people of Italy on the occasion of the centennial
shared_material.explanation: C05 has the strongest verbal and functional parallel, but the shared occasion/greetings/peoples formula is standard diplomatic language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the people of the United States join me in sending ... our best wishes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I send my greetings and best wishes, as well as those of the people of the United States ... to the people of Pakistan
shared_material.explanation: C18 closely parallels the sender, sentiment, and foreign national audience, but only through routine congratulatory phrasing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the people of the United States join me in sending to the peoples of the Soviet Union our best wishes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: express my appreciation and that of the people of the United States ... [for] the close friendship ... between our two countries
shared_material.explanation: C13 shares the President-plus-American-people diplomatic voice, but its purpose and operative content differ materially.
